reproduction_target: Two targets that must be scored together because the paper delivers both. (1) PIPELINE EXECUTABILITY READINESS of the Evidence Aggregator (EvAgg), an open-source, MIT-licensed Python pipeline that takes a query gene, retrieves candidate publications from the PubMed Central Open Access subset (PMC-OA) via NCBI E-utilities, filters them for data-mining-permissive licenses, decides relevance by consensus of keyword matching and a GPT-4-class LLM classifier, then extracts human genetic variant observations by a chain of LLM prompts (candidate entity identification, HGVS normalization via heuristics/regex, HGVS validation and consequence prediction via Mutalyzer v3, variant-to-individual linkage), and finally extracts per-observation phenotype (mapped to HPO terms), zygosity, variant type and inheritance, annotating with gnomAD v4.1 allele frequencies and publication metadata, emitting JSON that is surfaced as a table inside the seqr platform. (2) APPLICATION-LEVEL RESULTS: the reported evaluation numbers against an expert-curated gold-standard dataset (45 genes drawn from ClinGen submissions to GenCC; 4401 PubMed hits reviewed; 392 relevant papers; 224 observations over 167 variants in 41 papers; 70/30 gene-level dev/eval split; five replicate pipeline runs reported as mean and standard deviation; recall 0.92 paper selection, 0.96 variant-level, accuracy ~0.80 content extraction), the pre-/post-revision error analysis of 470 consistent disagreements, and the mixed-effects analysis of an IRB-approved A/B user study with eight rare-disease analysts (34% reduction in time per case, p<0.002). There is NO wet-lab component. The five non-computational steps enumerated below are human expert curation, blinded human adjudication, and human-subjects study execution/qualitative analysis; they are scored W/OOS by the same scope-split rule that removes wet-lab work from the denominator, and this substitution is stated explicitly rather than silently applied.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS source XML. FETCH NOTE: WebFetch of https://www.biorxiv.org/content/early/2025/11/10/2025.03.10.642480.source.xml returned HTTP 403; a direct curl with a browser User-Agent returned HTTP 200 / 106,613 bytes. The fetch was written to an isolated per-paper scratch directory (/tmp/stage1_10.1101_2025.03.10.642480/paper.xml) and identity was verified BEFORE scoring by grepping the title token 'Evidence Aggregator' (3 hits) and the DOI string '10.1101/2025.03.10.642480' in the fetched bytes; both matched, so no swap occurred. ROUTING: routed 'hybrid' because the paper ships a runnable open-source pipeline (tool-methods register: metric is pipeline executability readiness) AND makes application-level empirical claims that a reader would want to reproduce (evaluation metrics against a curated gold standard, error analysis, and a human-subjects user study with inferential statistics). A human reviewer may re-route to 'tool-methods' if the survey prefers to treat the shipped pipeline as the sole deliverable; that would drop C14-C19 from the denominator (S would fall from 19 to 13) and would REMOVE the two RI-scoring dataset-construction sampling steps and the RI-scoring evaluation/statistics steps, which would push the RI fraction DOWN, not up. The route is therefore not chosen to flatter the paper. STAGE-1 SCOPE: paper prose plus the repository landing page, README.md and SETUP.md prose only. No workflow source, no lib/config/*.yaml prompt or model spec, and no data/ file was read; every env_capture_class is 'n/a' and no step can reach R-star. VERSION CEILING - two independent reasons, both established at prose level and NOT merely the Stage-1 ceiling: (a) the repository ships environment.yml, a conda environment SPEC (not a lock) that pins ~45 direct dependencies with exact '==' (numpy==2.0.0, pandas==2.2.2, openai==1.35.10, httpx==0.27.0, biopython==1.84, pydantic==1.10.16, hpo3==1.3.1 via pip, etc.) but leaves the interpreter as a floating lower bound ('python>=3.12.4'), leaves poetry as '>=1.8.3', declares no platform, pins no channel index snapshot (channels are named conda-forge/defaults/bioconda only) and pins no transitive closure; poetry.lock is explicitly listed in .gitignore and is absent from the repository, and pyproject.toml states 'All package dependencies should be managed by conda' with the poetry package carrying only the local lib and no dependency section. That is exactly the exact_pins_partial pattern (version=1, never 2). (b) The paper cites the repository as a bare branch URL with no release tag, commit hash or Zenodo DOI, so 'the code that produced the numbers' is not fixed in time; two git tags exist upstream (v1.0.0-pre-testset, v1.0.0-pre-study) but neither is cited in the paper, and there are zero GitHub releases. PROPRIETARY CEILING (the dominant finding): the generative model is reached through a commercial, subscription-gated Azure OpenAI Service deployment. The paper names only the model family ('GPT-4-Turbo, which we used in most pipeline evaluation analyses') with no dated snapshot identifier bound to the reported results; SETUP.md specifies the requirement as a floating lower bound ('gpt-4 (1106-preview or newer), gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini') with an example .env value AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT="gpt-4-1106-preview" and AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION="2024-02-15-preview" annotated 'currently only tested against'. Model weights are not distributable and hosted snapshots are retired on the vendor's schedule, so the artefact that produced the results cannot be obtained by a third party. Under the Step-8 proprietary ceiling every LLM-dependent step is capped at NI regardless of axis-min; those steps are C5, C6, C9, C10, C11 and C18. This ceiling, not the environment, is what bounds this paper. STOCHASTICITY: the paper is explicit that the system is non-deterministic ('each paper appearing in ~89.3% of runs, showing stable performance despite LLM variability') and handles it the way ACM Artifact Badging permits, by reporting distributional match over five replicate runs as mean and standard deviation. No seed, temperature or top_p is stated in prose. The stochastic-no-seed ceiling (max RI, distributional-only) is therefore live for the LLM steps but is not binding, because the proprietary ceiling (NI) is lower. The two random-sampling steps of dataset construction (C14 gene draw, C16 paper draw and dev/eval split) also state no seed, but their OUTPUT - the realised sample - is published in the repository data/ directory, so a reader can reuse the exact sample even though they cannot regenerate the draw; those steps are RI with subflag distributional-only. DATA AXIS: data=2 throughout. Every input is public: PMC-OA full text, GenCC/ClinGen classifications (July 2024), gnomAD v4.1, HPO, and the paper's own generated artefacts are deposited in the repository ('Datasets generated and/or analyzed here are available in the GitHub repo data/ directory (curated dataset, user study quantitative data, error analysis results) and in supplementary information (user study qualitative data)'). No GEO/SRA/ENA/dbGaP/EGA accession exists or is needed - this is a literature-mining study with no sequencing data of its own. The human-subjects raw material (session recordings, interview transcripts) is de-identified per the IRB and is not deposited; that material feeds only W-layer steps, which are OOS.

steps.label: Candidate publication retrieval for each query gene from PubMed Central Open Access (PMC-OA) via REST calls to the NCBI E-utilities service, using the query string given verbatim in the paper: '<GENE SYMBOL> pubmed pmc open access[filter]'

License filtering of candidate publications: 'Candidate publications are further filtered to include only those whose licenses permit data mining and derivative use.' The specific license whitelist is not enumerated in the prose

Full-text acquisition for all retained publications via the BioC API ('All subsequent operations are performed on the full text of retrieved publications via the BioC API'); no BioC API version or access date is stated

Keyword-matching relevance filter over titles and abstracts using inclusion terms (examples given: 'mendelian', 'rare variant') and exclusion terms to remove non-monogenic disease and somatic cancer; the full term lists are deferred to Supplementary Methods and repository configuration

LLM-based paper relevance classification: a single prompt over title and abstract with four few-shot positive and four few-shot negative examples, combined with C4 by consensus, with the LLM re-run to break ties on disagreement. Executed against a subscription-gated Azure OpenAI deployment; the paper names only the model family 'GPT-4-Turbo' with no dated snapshot bound to the results

Observation finding, stage 1: LLM prompt chain (task decomposition with sequential prompts) identifying candidate entities - variant strings, metadata such as genome build and transcript IDs, and individual case identifiers - across the full text of each retained publication

Variant string normalization to HGVS nomenclature by heuristic filters and regular expressions, with consolidation of logically linked descriptions (e.g. DNA and protein forms of the same change) into a single entity. Deterministic, non-LLM; the heuristics and regexes are not reproduced in the prose

HGVS syntax and biological validity validation plus consequence prediction with Mutalyzer v3 (external web service; major version 'v3' stated, no point release, no access date, and no pin on the transcript reference data the service resolves against)

Variant-to-individual linkage forming patient-level observations, performed within the same sequential-prompt decomposition; papers in which no patient-level observation is found are discarded. The paper reports this as the weakest module (recall 0.75 with linkage vs 0.96 for variants alone), so it is load-bearing for the headline numbers

Content extraction of phenotype by individual or chained LLM prompts, with free-text descriptions mapped to Human Phenotype Ontology terms. The HPO release is explicitly NOT pinned - the repository states verbatim: 'The Evidence Aggregator uses the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO version dependent on user environment build and pipeline execution date/time)'

Content extraction of zygosity, variant type and inheritance pattern by individual or chained LLM prompts, against controlled value lists deferred to Supplementary Table 2. Inheritance is the weakest extracted field in the results (accuracy 0.52)
Annotation of each observation with gnomAD allele frequencies (version stated exactly as v4.1) and publication metadata

Output presentation: JSON emission from the pipeline, and integration of precomputed EvAgg outputs as a table behind an 'AI Evidence Aggregator' button in the seqr genomic analysis platform. The seqr-side integration code and UI are outside the EvAgg repository, no seqr version or commit is stated, and no deployment description is given

Gold-standard gene selection: start from 1900 genes submitted by ClinGen to GenCC, filter to 'Moderate', 'Limited' or 'No known GDR' classifications, then randomly select 15 genes from each of the three categories, yielding 45 genes. GenCC content snapshot dated in the repository as July 2024; no random seed stated, but the realised 45-gene sample is published in the repository data/ directory

PubMed search over the 45 selected genes returning 4401 results (mean 112.85, SD 92.65 papers per gene), focusing on publications appearing after the ClinGen expert-panel GDR approval. The search query string, search date and database snapshot for THIS search are not stated (unlike the pipeline query in C1)

Random sampling of at most two relevant papers per gene from the PMC-OA derivative-use-permitted subset, followed by a random 70/30 development/evaluation split performed on a per-gene basis. No seed stated; the realised split is published in the repository data/ directory, so the sample is reusable even though the draw is not regenerable

Pipeline evaluation metric computation against the curated dataset: recall and precision for paper selection and for observation finding (individual-plus-variant pairs), a variant-only recall variant computed by treating all individual identifiers as equivalent, exact-match accuracy for zygosity/variant type/inheritance, and generalized phenotype-category concordance; each evaluation run five times with mean and standard deviation reported, and all metrics reported for both the original and the post-error-analysis revised curated dataset. Paper states verbatim: 'Scripts to regenerate manuscript quantitative findings are available in the Github repo scripts/ directory'

Underlying-model comparison: 'a performance comparison of GPT-4-Turbo with other candidate LLMs as the underlying LLM used by the system', reported in Supplementary results. The competing models are not named anywhere in the retrievable main text, so neither the model set nor any snapshot identifier is recoverable at prose level

Mixed-effects modelling of user-study behavioural metrics: 'We used a mixed-effects model to analyze the impact of EvAgg on individual behavioral metrics, accounting for both fixed effects (study session and case set) and random effects (individual participants)', over time-stamped user actions and artifacts exported from seqr. No statistical package, model family, link function, estimation method or software version is named in the prose; the quantitative user-study data and the regeneration scripts are stated to be in the repository

NON-COMPUTATIONAL (human expert labour, scored OOS by the same rule that excludes wet-lab work): manual relevance assessment by the seven-person curation team of all 4401 PubMed results against a purpose-designed rubric, yielding 392 relevant papers (mean 10.05, SD 15.11 per gene)

NON-COMPUTATIONAL: manual per-observation content curation of the 41 papers containing variant observations (24 of 45 genes), extracting 224 unique observations over 167 variants - publication information, individual case identifiers, cDNA and protein HGVS annotation, variant type, genome build, transcript, zygosity, inheritance, free-text phenotype, HPO-encoded phenotype, study type and functional study information

NON-COMPUTATIONAL: blinded expert adjudication of the 470 consistent disagreements between EvAgg and the curated dataset (consistency defined as recurring across five independent pipeline runs), formatted as true/false or multiple-choice items, independently reviewed by two of three expert variant analysts blinded to source, with reviewer disagreements resolved by the broader curation team, followed by revision of the curated dataset

NON-COMPUTATIONAL (human subjects): execution of the A/B user study - eight trained analysts, two virtual recorded one-hour sessions on different days at the same start time, session 1 baseline and session 2 with EvAgg available, randomized fixed case order over two difficulty-matched sets of four unsolved Broad Rare Genomes Project cases with participants randomized to a set and crossed over on day two. IRB review by Microsoft Research IRB#1 (OHRP-IRB00009672, IORG0008066); informed consent obtained; participant data de-identified

NON-COMPUTATIONAL (human subjects): post-session Likert-scale surveys on usability, trust and overall experience, semi-structured participant interviews, and inductive thematic analysis of the survey and interview responses for emergent themes; two participants who had contributed to curated dataset generation were excluded from survey and interview analysis

headline.static_readiness: 0/19 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Applied symmetrically: this zero under-claims by construction - Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency, and has_validated_env_capture is false, so per-paper static_readiness is reported here only as the mandated ceiling statement and MUST NOT be read as a measurement of this paper's environment.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 12/19 (63%) RI, 7/19 (37%) NI, 0 X. The bound is set by one thing, and it is not the environment: it is the commercial generative model. Read the profile axis by axis. DATA is 2 everywhere - every input is public (PMC-OA full text, GenCC/ClinGen July 2024, gnomAD v4.1, HPO) and every artefact the paper generates is deposited: 'Datasets generated and/or analyzed here are available in the GitHub repo data/ directory (curated dataset, user study quantitative data, error analysis results)'. There is no accession to chase because there is no sequencing data; nothing is embargoed. CODE is 2 for fifteen of nineteen steps - the pipeline is MIT-licensed and public at https://github.com/cassimons/healthfutures-evagg, the README documents a four-step quickstart ending in a runnable sample pipeline, SETUP.md is a 224-line operational document covering Azure OpenAI provisioning, authentication, an optional CosmosDB response cache and a full .env template, and the paper separately commits scripts/ to regenerating the manuscript's quantitative findings. Code drops to 1 only for the three dataset-construction sampling steps (C14-C16, described in prose and Figure 2 but not tied to a named script) and for C13's seqr-side integration, which lives outside the repository. PARAMS is the quiet weakness: it is 1 for eighteen of nineteen steps, because the prompt texts, few-shot example sets, keyword inclusion/exclusion lists, controlled value lists, phenotype-category mapping and the mixed-effects model specification are all deferred to Supplementary Methods or to repository configuration rather than stated. Only C1 reaches 2, because the E-utilities query string is quoted verbatim. VERSION is 1 everywhere except C13 and C18 (0). Version never reaches 2 for a reason established at prose level and independent of the Stage-1 ceiling: environment.yml pins ~45 direct dependencies with exact '==' but leaves the interpreter as 'python>=3.12.4', declares no platform, pins no channel snapshot and no transitive closure, and poetry.lock is gitignored and absent - textbook exact_pins_partial. WHERE IT ACTUALLY STOPS: seven steps are NI, and six of those seven (C5, C6, C9, C10, C11, C18) are NI for a single shared reason - they call a GPT-4-class model through a subscription-gated Azure OpenAI deployment, identified in the paper only by family name ('GPT-4-Turbo, which we used in most pipeline evaluation analyses') and in SETUP.md only by a floating lower bound ('gpt-4 (1106-preview or newer), gpt-4o, and gpt-4o-mini'). The weights are not distributable and hosted snapshots are withdrawn on the vendor's schedule, so the artefact that produced the reported numbers cannot be obtained by a third party at any price. The Step-8 proprietary ceiling therefore caps these steps at NI regardless of their axis-min, which would otherwise have been RI. These six steps are not peripheral: they are paper selection, observation finding, variant-individual linkage and all content extraction - that is, the entire scientific claim. The seventh NI step, C13, is different in kind: the seqr integration that the user study actually put in front of participants is not deposited and no seqr version is stated. TWO SYMMETRIC CAVEATS. (a) This 63% may UNDER-state readiness: the repository is a well-maintained engineering artefact with a devcontainer, a Makefile with lint/test/ci targets, pytest unit tests, a dependency-injection configuration system with committed YAML specs under lib/config/, and a template.env - a Stage-2 read of those YAML specs could recover exact prompt texts, model deployment names and few-shot examples and lift Params on most LLM steps from 1 to 2. It could not, however, lift any of the six proprietary steps above NI, which is precisely why this paper is not a stage2_candidate. (b) It may also OVER-state readiness: the paper's own stability evidence ('each paper appearing in ~89.3% of runs') means roughly one in ten selected papers differs between runs even on identical inputs and an identical model, and the two mutable upstream corpora - PMC-OA, which grows continuously and for which no snapshot date is given, and HPO, which the repository explicitly says is 'version dependent on user environment build and pipeline execution date/time' - guarantee that a rerun today operates on different inputs. Neither effect is visible in the four axes.
headline.coverage: 19/19 computational steps (100% of the computational scope); 19/(19+5) = 79% computational coverage against the full method. Steps were enumerated from Materials and Methods (Pipeline overview, Paper selection, Observation finding, Content extraction, Presentation of pipeline outputs, Curated dataset, Pipeline evaluation, User study methods and measurements) of the bioRxiv v2 JATS source XML, one step per named tool or analysis invocation: 3 retrieval/acquisition steps (E-utilities, license filter, BioC API), 2 relevance-decision steps (keyword filter, LLM classifier plus consensus), 4 observation-finding steps (LLM entity identification, regex/heuristic HGVS normalization, Mutalyzer v3 validation, variant-individual linkage), 3 content-extraction/annotation steps (phenotype plus HPO, categorical fields, gnomAD v4.1 plus metadata), 1 output/integration step (JSON plus seqr), 3 dataset-construction steps (gene draw, PubMed search, paper draw plus dev/eval split), 2 evaluation steps (metric computation, candidate-LLM comparison) and 1 user-study statistics step (mixed-effects model). THIS PAPER HAS NO WET-LAB WORK. The five W-layer steps are human expert labour - rubric-based manual relevance review of 4401 papers, manual curation of 224 observations, blinded adjudication of 470 disagreements, execution of the IRB-approved eight-participant A/B study, and the survey/interview thematic analysis. They are scored OOS by the same scope-split rule that excludes wet-lab work, because they are equally outside the reach of a computational reproduction attempt; this substitution is recorded here explicitly so that a survey aggregating W counts across papers does not silently read '5' as 'five bench protocols'. Two consequences follow and are stated rather than buried. First, the gold-standard dataset against which all headline accuracy numbers are measured is itself a W product, and the paper's own error analysis found that EvAgg was more accurate than that gold standard in 235 of 470 disagreements (50%) - so the denominator of the reported metrics is known to be imperfect, which the authors handle honestly by reporting pre- and post-revision figures for everything. Second, the 34% time saving is a human-subjects finding with n=6 analysed participants; it is not reproducible from any artefact and no Tier-2 execution could confirm or refute it.

gaps.where: C5, C6, C9, C10, C11, C18 - every step that calls the generative model, i.e. paper relevance classification, entity identification, variant-individual linkage, phenotype extraction, categorical field extraction and the candidate-LLM comparison. This is the binding constraint on the whole paper
gaps.missing: The reasoning engine is a proprietary, subscription-gated, non-archivable commercial service, and it is not pinned. The paper's only identification is the model family: 'Future models may outperform GPT-4-Turbo, which we used in most pipeline evaluation analyses.' No dated snapshot identifier (e.g. gpt-4-0125-preview), no Azure OpenAI API version and no decoding parameters (temperature, top_p, seed, max_tokens, json-mode settings) are bound to the reported numbers anywhere in the prose. SETUP.md specifies the requirement as a floating lower bound - 'Current models that meet these two requirements are gpt-4 (1106-preview or newer), gpt-4o, and gpt-4o-mini' - with an example template value AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT="gpt-4-1106-preview" and AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION="2024-02-15-preview" annotated 'Note, currently only tested against'. It further requires the reader to provision their own Azure OpenAI resource with at least 100k TPM quota and a model supporting 128k input context and JSON output mode, i.e. a paid subscription is a hard precondition to any reproduction attempt. Model weights are not distributable and hosted snapshots are retired on the vendor's schedule, so the specific artefact that produced the results is not obtainable by a third party at any price or effort. Under the Step-8 proprietary ceiling these six steps cap at NI irrespective of axis-min, and they constitute the entire scientific pipeline. Compounding this, the system is explicitly non-deterministic ('each paper appearing in ~89.3% of runs, showing stable performance despite LLM variability') with no seed or temperature stated, so even a reader holding the identical deployment gets a different answer per run - the authors handle this correctly by reporting mean and standard deviation over five runs, which is the ACM-permitted distributional match, and that is why no step is driven to X.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact model deployment snapshot and the Azure OpenAI API version used for each reported table, alongside temperature, top_p, seed (if supported) and max_tokens, in the Methods or in a machine-readable run-config artefact committed next to the results. Deposit the raw LLM request/response logs for at least the eval-set run (the pipeline already writes debug files into .out/ per SETUP.md), so that the reported metrics can be recomputed from recorded model outputs even after the deployment is retired - this converts an unreproducible step into a verifiable one without requiring the model. Additionally, report a baseline on an open-weight model with a published checksum (the repository's dependency-injection design makes the client swappable), so that at least one fully reproducible configuration exists for the community, and archive the prompt set with the results.

gaps.where: Gap subtype 2a/2b (no environment-level version capture; floating lower bounds). Environment closure and code identity - all 19 computational steps
gaps.missing: No environment lock of any kind is shipped or claimed. The repository provides environment.yml, a conda environment SPECIFICATION, which does pin approximately 45 direct dependencies exactly (numpy==2.0.0, pandas==2.2.2, pyarrow==16.1.0, openpyxl==3.1.4, matplotlib==3.8.4, seaborn==0.13.2, plotly==5.22.0, pydantic==1.10.16, urllib3==2.2.2, azure-identity==1.17.1, openai==1.35.10, httpx==0.27.0, scikit-learn==1.5.1, biopython==1.84, pytest==8.2.2, and hpo3==1.3.1 under pip) but fails the environment-closure gate on four counts: the interpreter is a floating lower bound 'python>=3.12.4', the build tool is 'poetry>=1.8.3', no platform is declared (SETUP.md offers only prose - 'These instructions have been tested on Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 in WSL2 and on Azure VMs'), and channels are named (conda-forge, defaults, bioconda) without any index snapshot, leaving the entire transitive closure to be re-solved at install time. poetry.lock is explicitly listed in .gitignore and is absent from the repository; pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependency section, stating 'All package dependencies should be managed by conda'. Three type stubs use wildcard patch versions (types-requests==2.32.0.*). This is the exact_pins_partial pattern: version=1, never 2. Separately, code identity is not fixed in time - the paper cites a bare branch URL with no release tag, commit hash or Zenodo DOI. Two upstream tags exist (v1.0.0-pre-testset, v1.0.0-pre-study) but neither is cited in the paper and there are zero GitHub releases, so a reader cannot tell which tree state produced the numbers; the repository's last push observed at assessment time was 2025-08-25, after the v2 preprint's 2025-11-10 posting date carries no guarantee of tree stability either way.
gaps.how_to_close: Commit poetry.lock (the repository's own .gitignore comment already quotes the Poetry documentation recommending exactly this) or, better, generate a conda-lock for a declared platform (linux-64) that pins the interpreter to an exact patch version and records package URLs with hashes; alternatively record a container image digest, since a .devcontainer definition already exists in the repository and is one step away from a published, digest-addressed image. Tag the manuscript state of the code, archive that tag to Zenodo, and cite the tag plus DOI in the Data and code availability statement instead of the bare repository URL.

gaps.where: C1, C3, C8, C10, C12, C14, C15 - all external reference resources consumed out of band by the pipeline
gaps.missing: Every external knowledge source the pipeline reads is a live network service, and their pin quality is uneven and in one case explicitly absent. PMC-OA / NCBI E-utilities (C1) and the separate PubMed search used to build the gold standard (C15) are queried without any stated snapshot date, and the open-access corpus grows continuously, so the candidate paper set is not stable over time - this alone means the reported recall figures are computed against a corpus that no reader can reconstitute. The BioC API (C3) has no stated version or access date. Mutalyzer v3 (C8) is pinned only to a major version, and its validation and consequence-prediction results depend on transcript reference data that the service updates independently. HPO (C10) is the worst case and the authors state it plainly in the repository: 'The Evidence Aggregator uses the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO version dependent on user environment build and pipeline execution date/time)' - the ontology release is a function of when you happen to run, which is the mutable-latest pattern; note that the hpo3 library is pinned (hpo3==1.3.1) while the ontology data it loads is not, so a pinned dependency list gives false assurance here. gnomAD (C12) is the one clean pin: v4.1 is stated exactly. GenCC/ClinGen (C14) is dated to July 2024 in the repository README, which is a date but not an immutable versioned release. Whether each of these is fetched in code as a versioned artefact (class A), consumed from a user-supplied path with the version living only in prose (class B), or pulled rolling/latest (class C) can only be decided by reading the workflow, which is out of scope at Stage 1; env_capture_class is therefore n/a for every step and no R-star is awarded. The HPO statement above is strong prose evidence of class C, but it is not scored as such here.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and print, into the run output directory that the pipeline already creates, the resolved version of every external resource actually used in that run - the PMC-OA snapshot or search date, the BioC API version, the Mutalyzer service version and transcript release, the HPO release, the gnomAD version and the GenCC download date - and commit that resolved-versions file alongside each results table. Pin HPO to a specific dated release in configuration rather than resolving whatever is current at execution time. For the gold-standard construction, state the PubMed search date and the exact query string as was done for the pipeline query in C1.

gaps.where: C5, C6, C9, C10, C11, C18 (LLM stochasticity) and C14, C16 (unseeded random sampling in gold-standard construction)
gaps.missing: No random seed, temperature or sampling parameter is stated anywhere in the paper for any component. For the LLM steps the paper is transparent about the consequence and measures it - 'EvAgg consistently selected similar sets of papers, with each paper appearing in ~89.3% of runs' and 'Each evaluation was run five times, and we report the mean and standard deviation of the resulting metrics' - which satisfies the ACM distributional-match allowance, so these steps are flagged distributional-only rather than penalised further. For gold-standard construction the sampling is unseeded in two places: 'we randomly selected 15 genes from each category, yielding 45 genes' (C14) and 'We randomly selected at most two relevant papers for each gene from the PMC-OA subset' plus 'we randomly split the curated dataset into a development (dev) and evaluation (eval) set on a per gene basis. 70% of the genes were in the dev set' (C16). The mitigating fact, and the reason these stay RI, is that the realised samples are published in the repository data/ directory, so a reader can reuse the identical 45 genes, the identical selected papers and the identical dev/eval split without needing to regenerate the draw. What cannot be checked is whether the reported metrics are sensitive to the particular split - with only 45 genes and 13 or 14 genes in the eval set, split variance is plausibly comparable to the reported standard deviations.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and publish the seeds used for the gene draw, the paper draw and the dev/eval split so the construction is regenerable rather than merely reusable. Report metric variability across several dev/eval splits, or at minimum state the eval-set gene count next to each headline metric so readers can size the denominator. For the LLM steps, set and record a seed where the API supports it and record the decoding parameters used per run.

gaps.where: C13 (seqr integration and the user-study interface) and C19 (statistical analysis of the user study)
gaps.missing: Two analysis and integration components are described but not deposited or identified. C13: the paper states 'we have integrated the output as a table in the seqr platform' and the user study describes 'a simple user interface in the seqr variant search platform, where users could access an interactive table of precomputed EvAgg outputs by clicking an AI Evidence Aggregator button'. That interface is the artefact the eight participants actually used, and hence the object the 34% time-saving finding is about; it lives outside the EvAgg repository, no seqr version, commit or fork is stated, and no deployment description is given - so version=0 and code=1 for this step. C19: the analysis is specified only as 'a mixed-effects model ... accounting for both fixed effects (study session and case set) and random effects (individual participants)'. No statistical package, model family, link function, estimation method, degrees-of-freedom approximation or software version is named, and no model formula is written out, so the reported p-values (p<0.002 for time per case, p<0.02 for papers read, p=0.39 for manual searches) cannot be checked from the prose. The paper does state that regeneration scripts are in the repository scripts/ directory, which is why code=2 and the step stays RI rather than falling to NI; note also that environment.yml does not include a mixed-effects modelling package (no statsmodels, no lme4, no pymer4), which is a mild inconsistency worth a Stage-2 check.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the seqr integration as a fork or patch with a stated commit, or describe the rendered table precisely enough to be rebuilt, and state the seqr version used during the study. Write out the mixed-effects model formula and name the package and version used to fit it, and confirm that this package appears in environment.yml so that the regeneration scripts actually run in the declared environment.

gaps.where: W1-W5 - the five non-computational human-labour steps, and their consequence for how the C-layer numbers should be read
gaps.missing: Recorded as a scope statement, not as a penalty. The paper has no wet-lab component, but 5 of 24 enumerated steps are outside any computational reproduction attempt: rubric-based manual relevance review of 4401 papers by a seven-person curation team, manual curation of 224 observations across 41 papers, blinded expert adjudication of 470 EvAgg-versus-curation disagreements, execution of the IRB-approved eight-participant A/B study (Microsoft Research IRB#1, OHRP-IRB00009672, IORG0008066), and inductive thematic analysis of surveys and interviews. Two of these carry restricted material: session recordings and interview transcripts are de-identified per the IRB and are not deposited, so W4 and W5 are flagged controlled-access with data=1. The more consequential point is epistemic rather than procedural: the gold standard against which every headline accuracy figure is measured is itself a W product, and the paper's own error analysis found EvAgg more accurate than that gold standard in 235 of 470 disagreements (50%). The authors handle this well - the curation rubric is described, the disagreement review was blinded, and every metric is reported both pre- and post-revision - but a Tier-2 execution can only ever verify agreement with the deposited curated dataset, never the correctness of that dataset. Similarly the 34% time saving (n=6 analysed participants) is not reproducible from any artefact.
gaps.how_to_close: Nothing further is required of the authors for W1-W3 beyond what they already did, and the pre/post-revision dual reporting is exemplary practice worth naming as such. For W4-W5, publish the study protocol, the case-difficulty matching criteria and the survey and interview instruments verbatim as supplementary files so the study design is replicable even though the participant data cannot be shared, and state the analysed n next to each reported statistic (the text gives 8 enrolled and 2 excluded from survey/interview analysis, and the reader must infer which n applies to which figure).

gaps.where: C4, C5, C6, C7, C10, C11, C17 - prompts, term lists, regexes, value lists and mapping rules deferred to supplementary material or to repository configuration
gaps.missing: Params scores 1 rather than 2 on eighteen of nineteen steps, and the reason is uniform: the operative content of each step is not in the paper. The keyword filter gives two example inclusion terms ('mendelian', 'rare variant') and no exclusion terms, deferring the lists to Supplementary Methods. The LLM classifier is described as 'a single prompt ... with four few-shot positive and negative examples (see Supplementary Methods)' without the prompt text. The observation-finding prompt chain is characterised only as 'task decomposition with sequential prompts'. The HGVS normalization step applies unspecified 'heuristic filters and regular expressions'. Content extraction refers to 'individual or chained prompts' with value lists in Supplementary Table 2. Phenotype evaluation uses 'broader phenotypic categories (Supplementary methods)' whose mapping is the difference between the reported 0.80 exact accuracy and the 0.86 generalized concordance. The mitigating fact is real and is why these steps are not scored lower: the repository is public and organises exactly this content as committed YAML under lib/config/, resolved through a documented dependency-injection factory, so the material is very likely present in the code. Confirming that, and lifting Params to 2, is a Stage-2 read.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the prompt set, few-shot examples, keyword lists, normalization regexes and the phenotype-category mapping as a versioned appendix in the paper itself, or cite the exact repository file path and tag for each - a reader should not have to infer which lib/config YAML corresponds to which Methods sentence. Since prompts are the method here in the same sense that a command line is the method in a conventional pipeline, quoting them in the Methods is the direct analogue of quoting the E-utilities query string, which the paper already does well in C1.

gaps.where: The single code and data URL on which everything depends: https://github.com/cassimons/healthfutures-evagg
gaps.missing: Recorded as a fragility, not as a current failure - the URL resolves 200 at assessment time. The repository has been transferred out of the Microsoft organisation into a personal account: the paper's stated URL is https://github.com/cassimons/healthfutures-evagg, while the repository's own README still instructs 'git clone https://github.com/microsoft/healthfutures-evagg', which currently works only because GitHub serves an owner-rename redirect. That redirect is not durable - it breaks permanently if anyone creates a new repository at microsoft/healthfutures-evagg - and personal-account hosting is weaker stewardship than organisational hosting for an artefact that carries both the code and the sole copy of the curated dataset. There is no Zenodo deposit, no Software Heritage archive, no release and no cited tag, so a single account action would take the code, the gold-standard dataset, the user-study quantitative data and the error-analysis results offline simultaneously. No redundancy rescue is available because no authoritative mirror exists.
gaps.how_to_close: Archive a tagged release to Zenodo (or Software Heritage) and cite that DOI in the Data and code availability statement so the artefact survives repository moves; update the README clone command to the current canonical URL so it does not depend on a redirect. Consider depositing the curated dataset separately to a data repository, since it is explicitly offered as a community resource ('We hope this dataset can support the broader community's efforts') and deserves an identifier independent of the code.
